ch20.d.N: Number of gas particles in the box
ch20.e.goal.S: Entropy $S = k\ln\Omega$: the log of the number of microstates $\Omega$ allowed by a macrostate (particles $n$ in the left half)
ch20.e.goal.irr: Statistical origin of irreversibility: the gas moves to the macrostate with the most microstates ($n \approx N/2$) and almost never comes back
ch20.e.obs.peak: $\Omega(n)$ bars: largest at $n = N/2$; the highlighted bar is the current macrostate
ch20.e.obs.small: $N = 4$: all particles often gather in the left half again (probability $1/2^4 = 1/16$)
ch20.e.obs.large: $N = 1000$: probability $1/2^{1000} \approx 10^{-301}$, so the initial state never returns in practice; $n$ only fluctuates by about $\sqrt N/2$ around $N/2$
ch20.e.obs.S: $\Delta S(t)$: rises quickly, then fluctuates just below its maximum $\Delta S_\text{max}$. For large $N$, $\Delta S_\text{max} \to Nk\ln 2$, the thermodynamic free-expansion result $nR\ln(V_f/V_i)$ ($N = 1000$: 689.5 vs 693.1)
ch20.e.assume: Particles do not collide with each other (ideal gas) and reflect perfectly from the walls and the partition. All start on the left; the user removes the partition
ch20.e.assume.ref: Entropy reference: the all-left state ($\Omega = 1$) is set to zero. Only the left/right arrangement is counted, so this is not the absolute entropy (counting positions within each half and velocities too, the initial state has $S > 0$). Only the change $\Delta S$ is physical
ch20.assume.omegaW: $\Omega$: multiplicity (number of microstates; the textbook's $W$). In this chapter $W$ is used only for the work of the Carnot cycle
ch20.h.d.na: Number of oscillators in solid A; solid B has the rest ($N_\text{A} + N_\text{B} = 100$)
ch20.h.d.q: Total number of energy quanta $\varepsilon$ shared by the two solids
ch20.h.d.start: Solid that holds every quantum at the start (the other is at $T = 0$)
ch20.h.goal.flow: Heat flows in the direction that increases the total number of microstates $\Omega_\text{A}\Omega_\text{B}$, that is, from hot to cold
ch20.h.goal.T: Equilibrium: $S_\text{tot}$ is largest, so $\partial S_\text{A}/\partial E_\text{A} = \partial S_\text{B}/\partial E_\text{B}$; this defines temperature, $1/T = \partial S/\partial E$
ch20.h.obs.flow: Quanta hop at random both ways, but the net flow goes from the solid that starts with all the quanta to the other (hot to cold) and $S_\text{tot}$ rises
ch20.h.obs.max: $S$-$q_\text{A}$ diagram: the current state (dot) climbs to the top of the $S_\text{tot}$ curve
ch20.h.obs.slope: At the top the tangents of $S_\text{A}$ and $S_\text{B}$ have equal and opposite slopes, so $kT_\text{A} = kT_\text{B}$. With few quanta the top sits on a whole-number $q_\text{A}$ and the slopes agree only roughly ($N_\text{A} = 10$, $q = 20$: $q_\text{A} = 1$, about 12 % apart)
ch20.h.obs.size: $N_\text{A} = 30$, $N_\text{B} = 70$ (default): at equilibrium the energies are not equal ($q_\text{A} \approx 30$); the temperatures are
ch20.h.obs.fluct: After equilibrium $q_\text{A}$ keeps fluctuating, but $S_\text{tot}$ stays near its maximum
ch20.h.assume.model: Einstein solid: an oscillator is one atom of the solid vibrating along one direction (a ball on a spring), all at the same frequency. An oscillator's energy can only be a whole number of energy quanta $\varepsilon = hf$ ($0, \varepsilon, 2\varepsilon, \dots$)
ch20.h.assume.omega: Number of microstates $\Omega(N, q)$: the number of ways to share $q$ quanta among $N$ oscillators (3 oscillators, 2 quanta: 6 ways). One random move: one oscillator passes one quantum to another, so every microstate is equally likely
ch20.h.assume.slope: Why the slope gives the temperature: heat $dQ$ entering changes the entropy by $dS = dQ/T$ (the thermodynamic definition), so $\partial S/\partial E = 1/T$. With $E = q\varepsilon$ the slope on the diagram is $d(S/k)/dq = \varepsilon/kT$: steep means cold, shallow means hot. The tangents use the exact slope of the curve, $1/(q+1) + \dots + 1/(q+N-1)$
ch20.h.assume.T: The readouts and the $kT/\varepsilon$ graph use the large-$N$ form $kT/\varepsilon = 1/\ln(1 + N/q)$, with $q_\text{A}$ averaged over 1.5 s (a thermometer's response time). With few quanta this differs slightly from the exact slope of the tangents
ch20.h.assume.arrow: $Q$ arrow: shown only for a net heat flow that fluctuations cannot explain. It depends on how far the 1.5 s average of $q_\text{A}$ lies from its equilibrium value $qN_\text{A}/N$: shown when equilibrium fluctuations reach that far less than 0.5 % of the time, hidden above 2 %. It points towards equilibrium, from the hotter to the colder displayed temperature. If the starting state is a common fluctuation at equilibrium too, no arrow appears ($N_\text{A} = 10$, $q = 20$, all in B: $q_\text{A} = 0$ also 15 % of the time at equilibrium)
ch20.c.d.tc: Temperature of the cold reservoir that takes the waste heat (hot reservoir at 600 K)
ch20.c.goal.limit: Efficiency of a Carnot engine $e = 1 - T_\text{C}/T_\text{H}$: the upper limit for any engine working between two reservoirs
ch20.c.goal.ts: On a $T$-$S$ diagram the Carnot cycle is a rectangle: area under the path = heat, enclosed area = net work
ch20.c.obs.legs: A→B isothermal expansion (takes in $Q_\text{H}$), B→C adiabatic expansion, C→D isothermal compression (gives off $Q_\text{C}$), D→A adiabatic compression
ch20.c.obs.first: Bars: first law, $W = Q_\text{H} - Q_\text{C} - \Delta E_\text{int}$, with $W$ the work done by the gas. On the adiabatic expansion B→C the gas does work with no heat, at the cost of internal energy, so $W > Q_\text{H}$ (defaults, at C: $W = 2886$ J, $Q_\text{H} = 1386$ J, $\Delta E_\text{int} = -1500$ J). When the loop closes, $\Delta E_\text{int} = 0$ and $W = Q_\text{H} - Q_\text{C}$
ch20.c.obs.ratio: The two isotherms span the same entropy change, so $Q_\text{C}/Q_\text{H} = T_\text{C}/T_\text{H}$ and the gas has $\Delta S = 0$ over a cycle
ch20.c.obs.tc: Lowering $T_\text{C}$ raises the efficiency (200 K: 0.667, 400 K: 0.333)
ch20.c.obs.gas: Diatomic gas: the $p$-$V$ loop changes shape but the efficiency is the same
ch20.c.assume.ideal: Ideal gas, about 0.401 mol, A: 10 L, 600 K
ch20.c.assume: Quasi-static, reversible steps; reservoirs large enough to keep their temperatures; no friction
ch20.e.obs.remove: At first the gas is in the left half behind the partition ($n = N$, $\Omega = 1$, $\Delta S = 0$). Press "Remove partition" under the box, or the partition itself, to remove it and let the gas spread to the right. Reset (R) puts the partition back
